entries.text_de:
Aus der Bibliothek des Coxe Macro kam 1820 die früher Fleetwood12, dann Spelman13 gehörige, älteste, um 1150 geschriebene Quadripartitus-Hs. an die Familie Gurney zu Keswick Hall bei Norwich14.

Der Band begann im 16. Jh. wie Hk mit Cn, u. S. 279, und enthielt f. 12b Af, u. S. 17. Aus diesen Anfangsblättern vermuthlich notirte ein Antiquar des 16. Jahrhunderts auf ein vorgeheftetes Papierblatt als Titel Quadripartitus. Jetzt fehlen die Folien 1—20. Fol. 21 beginnt baptismo: Ine 2, 1, u. S. 91; f. 49b I. II As, u. S. 147. 151; f. 52b Episc, u. S. 477; f. 53 Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, u. S. 459—65; f. 54 Blas, Forf, u. S. 389; f. 54b Hu, u. S. 192; f. 55 IV As, u. S. 171; f. 56 V As, u. S. 167; f. 56b III As, u. S. 170; f. 57b VI As, u. entries.text_en:
From the library of Coxe Macro there came in 1820 to the Gurney family at Keswick Hall near Norwich14 the oldest Quadripartitus MS, written c. 1150, which formerly belonged to Fleetwood12, then to Spelman13.

In the 16th century the volume began, like Hk, with Cn, below, p. 279, and contained f. 12b Af, below, p. 17. Probably from these opening leaves an antiquary of the 16th century noted the title Quadripartitus on a paper leaf bound in front. Now folios 1—20 are missing. Fol. 21 begins baptismo: Ine 2, 1, below, p. 91; f. 49b I. II As, below, pp. 147. 151; f. 52b Episc, below, p. 477; f. 53 Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, below, pp. 459—65; f. 54 Blas, Forf, below, p. 389; f. 54b Hu, below, p. 192; f. 55 IV As, below, p. 171; f. 56 V As, below, p. 167; f. 56b III As, below, p. 170; f. 57b VI As, below, p. 173; f. 61 Ordal, below, p. 386; f. 61 I Atr, below, p. 217; f. 62 III Atr, below, p. 228; f. 63b Pax, Wal, IV Atr, II Atr, below, pp. 391. 393. 232. 221; f. 66b Duns, below, p. 375; f. 67b VII Atr, below, p. 260; f. 68b Iudex, below, p. 474; f. 69 II. III Eg, below, p. 195; f. 70b AGu, below, p. 127; f. 71 App. AGu, below, p. 394; f. 71b EGu, below, p. 129; f. 73b I. II Ew, below, p. 139; f. 74b I Em, below, p. 185; f. 75 III Em, below, p. 190; f. 75b II Em, below, p. 187; f. 76 Swer, below, p. 397; f. 77 Wif, below, p. 443; f. 77b Wer, below, p. 393; f. 78 Wl lad, below, p. 483; f. 78 Geþyncðo, below, p. 457; f. 78b Rect, below, p. 444; f. 81b CHn cor, below, p. 521; f. 82b Quadr II 4—8, 3, below, p. 544; f. 83b De archidiaconibus1; f. 84 Hn com, below, p. 524.

A somewhat later hand adds Stephen’s charter of Dec. 1153 for the succession of Henry II2.

wormald.shelfmark: Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Lat. 420
wormald.wormald_origin: Origin and provenance unknown until perhaps in the library of Sir Henry Sidney c. 1580 (Nowell's 'libro domini Sydney' probably M, p. 238 n. 305); later studied by Spelman (p. 237)
wormald.laws: Quadripartitus (final MHk recension): (I–II Cn, Af lost) …Ine, I–II As, Episc, Norðleod, Mirce, Að, Had, Blas, Forf, Hu, III–VI As, Ordal, I/III Atr, Pax, Wal, IV Atr, II Atr, Duns, VII Atr, Iudex, II–III Eg, AGu, App. AGu, EGu, I–II Ew, I–III Em, Swer, Wif, Wer, Wl lad, Geþyncðo, Rect; Part II: CHn cor, Quadr. II 4–8:3, 18, Hn com; added 1153 treaty (Tr. Winch.) (Table 4.7, pp. 240–1)

wormald.other_contents: Plain, compact volume, script said to have 'notarial elements' (Rumble); appendix of Stephen's 1153 treaty recognizing his successor; first two quires lost, but 16th-century contents list shows it began with Cnut and lacked the prefaces (pp. 238–9).
wormald.overview: A mid-twelfth-century copy of the final, considered recension of Quadripartitus, now in Manchester, which agrees in every particular with Hk; together they are the nearest surviving approach to the author's finished edition. Its opening quires are lost, and the 1153 settlement between Stephen and Henry was added as an appendix. Its known history begins only around 1580, perhaps in Sir Henry Sidney's library.
wormald.key_quote: MHk looks very like the nearest that surviving manuscripts offer to a final version, though M is the second oldest manuscript. (p. 243)
wormald.doubts: GUIDE: the guide gives the location as Keswick Hall, Norwich (Gurney family, 1903); Wormald gives the current shelfmark Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Lat. 420. GUIDE: Liebermann (guide notes) called M 'the oldest Quadripartitus manuscript (c. 1150)'; Wormald makes Dm (s. xii^2/4) the earliest and M the second oldest.
